newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rebound, but finance jitters linger.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rebound, but finance jitters linger.

text.p: Thailand's stock market staged a surprise recovery on Tuesday after three successive sessions of decline, but concern over the failing health of finance companies and the country's economic slowdown lingered on.
The SET Index fell by more than 1.5 percent in early trade, but it turned around in afternoon trade to end 1.48 points, or 0.26 percent, higher at 569.84.
Traders said there appeared to be more two-way business than on Monday, when a crash of the exchange's trading system left players with just 33 minutes to join a selling spree.

Some suspected that local mutual funds rather than the commercial bank-backed market support fund had bought stocks on Tuesday, though more than one fund manager said the market remained unattractive.
"There is a list of negative factors as long as your arm," said one. "But it depends on your time horizon, and for us the time is not right."
The market, languishing at eight-year lows, started on its latest downturn ahead of last Friday's news that plans for a merger between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc had collapsed.
Analysts said the news dented confidence in the authorities' ability to solve liquidity and bad debt problems faced by many of the country's 91 finance firms.
The biggest of those firms and once a darling of the market, Finance One said last week that it had suffered a 3.75 billion ($145.3 million) loss for the first quarter alone.
After the merger fell through, the central Bank of Thailand ordered Finance One to raise its capital by 8.28 billion baht ($320.9 million) through a two-for-one rights issue.
The stock exchange said it would allow trading in the company's shares, suspended when the merger talks were first announced three months ago, to resume on Friday.
Traders said Finance One's shares were quoted at three to four baht in the unofficial "grey market" compared with 23.75 when trade was halted on February 28.
The baht, whose recent wobble on speculative attacks has made it another drag on the stock market, was stable on Tuesday as dollar buying waned with the U.S. currency's generally weaker tone.
The baht ended unchanged at 25.810/25.840 per dollar on the onshore market after slipping to 25.85 earlier in the day.

The two-tier money market system imposed by the central bank last week to stave off offshore speculative attacks on the baht remained intact, and the central bank said on Tuesday that it would review the regime from time to time.
Under the system, the Bank of Thailand cut baht supplies to the offshore players by asking Thailand-based commercial banks to lend baht to foreign parties only at punitive rates.
